transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, thank you for calling S-Net security and technical support. My name is Freya. How may I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh hello Freya, my name is Svetlana. My hands are literally shaking right now—a man just phoned my landline claiming to be from S-Net technical support and said hackers were inside my router, and I'm terrified he's gotten into my pension bank account!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for letting me know, Svetlana. Let's get your account verified right away so I can inspect your security logs. Could you please confirm your full postal address and your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, of course, it's 19 Meadowcroft Close, Harrogate, HG2 8PL, and my four-digit PIN is 5528. Oh dear, my heart is racing so fast, I live on my own and you read such awful stories in the paper.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Svetlana, that PIN and address are confirmed on your profile. To summarize what has happened, an unknown caller claiming to represent S-Net rang you about alleged router compromise, and you want us to verify your account is untouched and lock down all of your passwords today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's exact! He had a very pushy voice and told me my Hub 4 was broadcasting my bank details to the street, and demanded I sit at my iPad right away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I run the audit on your line, Svetlana, I need to ask a few specific diagnostic questions so we know exactly what exposure existed. Did you read out your S-Net PIN, your bank card numbers, or any one-time passcodes to that caller?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, thank heavens, when he asked me to open Safari on my iPad and type in a strange web link starting with 'anydesk', I remembered what my nephew told me and I put the receiver straight down!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is very helpful detail, Svetlana. And just to be thorough, did you type that 'anydesk' address into Safari at all, or click any text message links, or was the iPad screen completely untouched before you disconnected the call?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I didn't type a single letter into the iPad—I hadn't even unlocked the screen when I decided his voice sounded wrong and ended the call, and then I dialled 150 from my landline to reach you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And did the caller display show a specific telephone number on your Harrogate landline handset when he rang, Svetlana, and roughly what time did the call come through?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my cordless screen showed 0161 496 0821 at 10:15 this morning. Honestly, I feel so silly for even staying on the line with him for two minutes, my knees still feel weak.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I have noted the 0161 496 0821 caller ID at 10:15 AM and the fact that no 'anydesk' link was opened on your iPad and no bank or PIN digits were shared.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could he have gotten into my S-Net account or my router just by knowing my landline number and my surname?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No external caller can access your Hub 4 or your My S-Net billing portal solely from a public directory number, Svetlana, and S-Net never cold-calls customers asking them to install remote-control tools like AnyDesk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that is a relief to hear, though I still won't rest easy until every single log and password on my account has been checked from top to bottom.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, Svetlana, did the caller mention any specific details from your S-Net bill, such as your account number or your package name, or did he only know your surname and landline number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: He only said 'Mrs Kovacs' and my landline number—when I asked him what my S-Net account number was, he dodged the question and shouted that my router would burn out if I didn't hurry!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms he was working from a public telephone directory list rather than any S-Net database, Svetlana.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm still trembling a little bit just thinking about how aggressive he was on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will take care of the entire security sweep for you right now, Svetlana. Please bear with me for a moment while I inspect your My S-Net portal login history, your router TR-069 management log, and your billing mandate records.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, Freya, I will stay right here on the line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Svetlana. I have completed a full audit of your My S-Net portal, your Harrogate fibre line, and your Hub 4 remote management records.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what did you find, Freya? Has anyone logged in or touched my pension Direct Debit details?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Everything on your account is completely clean, Svetlana. The last login to your My S-Net online portal was eighteen days ago from your own Harrogate home IP address, and there have been zero failed login attempts and zero changes to your Direct Debit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about the Hub 4 router in my hallway? The man on the 0161 number claimed he could see red warning alerts coming off my Wi-Fi!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That was a fabricated claim used by telephone scammers, Svetlana. Your Hub 4 telemetry shows normal encrypted WPA2 traffic with only two connected devices on your home network: your Apple iPad and your smart television.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Only my iPad and my telly! He was lying through his teeth the whole time! Still, could we change both my My S-Net password and my Wi-Fi password right now just so I know it's locked tight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, Svetlana, I will handle both of those updates with you on this call, and I will also add an extra verbal security password to your telephone account and report 0161 496 0821 to our fraud nuisance database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, thank you, Freya, you are so patient and clear with me. Let's do the verbal telephone password first if we can.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Certainly, Svetlana. Along with your four-digit PIN 5528, we can set a memorable security question and word that any agent must ask before discussing your account. What memorable word would you like me to register?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could we make the memorable question 'What was the name of your first cat?' and the answer 'Marmalade'?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have saved 'What was the name of your first cat?' with the answer 'Marmalade' on your high-security account banner right now, Svetlana.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that mean if anyone rings up pretending to be me, they won't get anywhere without saying 'Marmalade'?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is right, Svetlana—every S-Net advisor sees a mandatory prompt requiring both your PIN and the answer 'Marmalade' before opening your billing or technical tabs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wonderful. Now how do we change my My S-Net online password on my iPad?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have just triggered an official password reset link to your registered email address on file, Svetlana, and I can see you have your iPad nearby—take all the time you need to open your mail app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me put my reading glasses on... yes, the email from S-Net Account Security has just popped up at the top of my inbox!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, Svetlana. Tap the blue 'Create New Password' button inside that email, and enter a new passphrase that is at least twelve characters long with a capital letter and a number—please do not read the password aloud to me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm typing a brand-new fourteen-letter phrase in both boxes now... let me make sure both lines match...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take all the time you need, Svetlana. Once both boxes match, tap the green 'Save Changes' button underneath.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've tapped 'Save Changes' now. It says 'Your My S-Net password has been updated'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the new credential hash registered on our authentication server at this exact second, Svetlana, and I have also invalidated all older browser tokens.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Would you recommend turning on two-step verification on my My S-Net account as well, Freya?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Svetlana, enabling SMS two-factor authentication is an excellent layer of protection. Would you like me to switch that on for your mobile number ending in 309?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please! My mobile ending 309 is always in my cardigan pocket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have just sent a six-digit verification code to your mobile ending in 309 to bind two-factor authentication to your profile, Svetlana. Can you read me that six-digit code when it arrives?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It just pinged! The six-digit code is 841-902.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Svetlana, 841-902 is verified and SMS two-factor authentication is now active on your My S-Net login.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That was so straightforward when you talked me through it step by step! Now what about changing the Wi-Fi password on my Hub 4 router?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Rather than making you log into the router admin page, Svetlana, I can push a new WPA2 Wi-Fi passphrase directly to your Hub 4 from my console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, you can do that remotely from your screen? How will I know what the new Wi-Fi password is without reading it aloud over the phone?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated tool generates a fresh random twelve-character passphrase and sends it directly via encrypted SMS to your registered mobile ending in 309, Svetlana. Shall I generate and push that now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sending the fresh generated Wi-Fi passphrase by text message to my mobile phone sounds much safer! Yes please, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have pushed the new WPA2 key to your Hub 4 and dispatched the SMS to your mobile ending in 309, Svetlana. Your Hub 4 Wi-Fi radio will blink for about ten seconds while it applies the new key.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The text message just arrived on my mobile! And I can see the little Wi-Fi fan icon on my iPad just dropped off as expected.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now open Settings and tap Wi-Fi on your iPad, Svetlana, select your 'S-Net-Hub4-8PL' network, tap 'Forget This Network', and then tap it again to enter the new twelve-character key from your text message.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've tapped Forget This Network... now tapping S-Net-Hub4-8PL again and typing in the code from the text message... one moment...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take your time typing those characters, Svetlana, there is no rush at all.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm on the last four characters now... and tapping Join.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me watch the DHCP table on your Hub 4 while it handshakes with your iPad, Svetlana.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There we go, I've got the blue tick next to S-Net-Hub4-8PL and the Wi-Fi bars are back at the top corner of my iPad!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: My console confirms your iPad has re-authenticated on the new WPA2 key, Svetlana, and is passing encrypted traffic normally.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me just tap on BBC News on my iPad to be one hundred percent sure the internet page loads... yes, the headlines came straight up!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic, Svetlana. I have also added the spoofed number 0161 496 0821 to your S-Net Call Shield blocklist and activated Network-Level Scam Call Protection on your Harrogate landline free of charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You've blocked that 0161 number and switched on Scam Call Protection on my landline as well? Oh, Freya, you have thought of everything!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Svetlana, any known spoofed or overseas CLI pretending to be a UK local exchange will now be intercepted at our network switch before your hallway telephone even rings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I just double-check—will my smart television need the new Wi-Fi code from my text message when I switch it on this evening for the news?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Svetlana, when you turn on the television tonight, go to Network Settings, select 'S-Net-Hub4-8PL', and enter that same twelve-character code from your mobile SMS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've written it down neatly in my address book next to the television remote so I won't lose it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you ever want to add another number to your Call Shield blocklist from your landline handset, Svetlana, you can simply dial 1572 after any unwanted call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dial 1572—I've jotted that down right next to the Wi-Fi code in my notebook.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To confirm everything is resolved for you today, Svetlana: your account audit showed zero unauthorized access, your My S-Net password, 2FA, and verbal codeword 'Marmalade' are active, your iPad is online with the new Wi-Fi key, and Call Shield is enabled. Are you happy that everything is sorted?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, everything is completely sorted and working, and I know my account and my iPad are safe. Thank you so much for your help today, Freya.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome, Svetlana. Thank you for choosing S-Net, and enjoy the rest of your day. Goodbye!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye, Freya!
